headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from Cline’s workspace/MCP access into social-auto-upload’s API-driven publishing flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads workspace files and uses MCP/browsers, while social-auto-upload consumes files and account data for uploads. A malicious file or caption in the shared workspace could influence Cline’s tool use and then be carried into B’s publishing inputs. The bridge is plausible in default workspace-based use, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF B ingests text or metadata produced by A without sanitization
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers for Cline unless needed
Require manual review of any text passed from A to B
Use a file allowlist for B inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline can read broad filesystem content and handle model-provider API keys; social-auto-upload touches account data and uploads media files. If they share a workspace or account files, Cline may expose sensitive content into B’s upload context or logs. The profiles do not show PHI, but account data and source code are enough for a meaningful leakage pathway.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem tree
IF B logs or uploads file contents from the shared tree
mitigations: Store account files outside the shared workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys or account secrets
Restrict Cline to a read-only clone when inspecting B inputs
Review B’s upload manifest before execution
requires-engineering: isolate secrets with per-agent vaults

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted write, git, shell, and network capabilities; social-auto-upload has no filesystem write or shell capability. Their write surfaces do not overlap by profile, so direct resource contention is limited. The only plausible conflict is indirect through shared workspace files, which is narrower than the rubric’s medium/high cases.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF B is extended to write account files into that directory
mitigations: Run B in a separate directory
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Use git branches for A’s changes
Serialize file writes with a simple operator checklist

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, or file edits that social-auto-upload may treat as upload-ready artifacts. Because B has API-facing publishing behavior and no verification mechanism is shown, A’s output can cascade into B’s actions with limited checking. This is not high because the profiles do not prove autonomous irreversible actions, but the default handoff is still risky.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated captions, metadata, or media manifests
IF no human review occurs between A’s output and B’s upload call
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before upload
Compare A’s output against source files
Limit B to draft-only mode when possible
Log the exact artifact hash passed from A to B
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A-to-B handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the visible data classes are source code, browser screenshots, video, images, and account data. No explicit residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary account-data handling. I do not cite only one agent because the issue is the pair’s combined data flow, but the evidence is sparse.
conditions: IF account data from B is stored in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from the operator’s policy
IF A’s browser screenshots capture regulated content
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both tools
Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces
Review where account files are stored
Delete transient screenshots after use
